name: NanoClaw
vibe_summary: A security-first, radically minimal OpenClaw alternative that runs each agent in its own Linux container with real OS-level isolation. Built on Anthropic's Agents SDK with multi-channel messaging, memory, and scheduled jobs in a codebase small enough to actually read.
best_for: Security-conscious users who want OS-level agent isolation
Developers who want a small, auditable codebase
Teams deploying per-agent Slack bots with separate identities
Users already invested in Anthropic's Agents SDK
avoid_if: You need model-provider flexibility beyond Anthropic-first design
You want a large plugin ecosystem and mature community tooling
You can't run Docker/containers on your host
You need OpenClaw's breadth of integrations and UI features
openclaw_advantages: True container-level isolation instead of application-level permission checks
Dramatically smaller codebase that one person can fully audit
Fewer dependencies and config files means smaller attack surface
Per-agent Slack apps with isolated identities, containers, and memory
Guided setup script with automatic failure diagnosis
openclaw_disadvantages: Far fewer integrations, skills, and community extensions
Smaller community and shorter track record
Tightly coupled to Anthropic's Agents SDK and Claude
Lacks OpenClaw's Control UI and broader platform polish
Container requirement adds host prerequisites OpenClaw doesn't have

overview_markdown:
NanoClaw is a security-first rethinking of OpenClaw built around one core idea: agents should run in their own Linux containers with filesystem isolation, not behind application-level allowlists in a shared Node process. Where OpenClaw has grown to nearly half a million lines with 53 config files and 70+ dependencies, NanoClaw deliberately stays small — one process and a handful of files — so a single operator can read and understand everything it does before trusting it with their accounts.

Architecturally it runs directly on Anthropic's Agents SDK and connects to Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, iMessage, Gmail, and a local CLI, with persistent memory, scheduled jobs, and per-agent group configuration (model, effort, and speed tiers). A standout feature is its Slack integration: setup provisions each agent its own Slack app with a manifest, avatar, and workspace install, so spawned teammates get distinct bot identities, containers, and memory. Recent commits show an active refactor toward a formal provider contract system — runtime, host, and setup seams are now declared as executable contracts verified by an install-time verifier, suggesting the project is hardening its extension points for multi-provider support beyond Claude.

Compared to OpenClaw, NanoClaw trades breadth for trust: you give up the massive integration ecosystem, Control UI, and model flexibility in exchange for a codebase you can audit in an afternoon and isolation enforced by the OS rather than by convention. The `nanoclaw.sh` quick-start script handles dependency installation, credential registration via OneCLI, container builds, and channel pairing — even invoking Claude Code to self-diagnose failed steps — making it one of the more approachable secure agent setups available.
